text:
Riley Gomez: Pushing a fresh pass on latency card layout in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/latency-v5 — want to lock down microcopy + small-screen p95 behavior :mag_right:
Omar Khan: looks great overall. main friction I saw: when user zooms into short ranges (<3m) the p95 chip overlaps the scrubber thumb and the value gets clipped
Zoe Chen: thought: collapse the chip to a tiny glyph that still announces the value to assistive tech. on hover/tap show a compact tooltip like "p95: 198ms"
Marta Diaz: thumbs up for aria approach. prefer explicit aria-label text rather than hiding visible text with CSS hacks
Riley Gomez: agreed. alternative microcopy suggestions for sampling control — current label is confusing (`Show samples`). propose using `Sample density` with a short suffix line explaining tradeoffs
Omar Khan: what options?
Riley Gomez: Auto (balanced), High (more tokens sampled, higher cost), Economy (sparse sampling, lower cost)
Marta Diaz: accessibility note: screen readers should read the sublabel for the selected density. e.g., `Sample density, Auto, optimizes between latency and cost`
Zoe Chen: heatmap UX: when sample density is low the buckets look like missing data. we should render a stippled overlay on low-density buckets and a tiny legend pill that says `stippled = sparsely sampled`
Riley Gomez: love 'stippled' phrasing. let's use microcopy under the heatmap: `Stippled buckets indicate low sample density; results may be noisy.` link to docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/observability/sampling
Design Bot: snapshot saved for 2141599999 (latency-v5-preview)
Omar Khan: keyboard bug: when opening the time range popover, tab cycle goes: presets -> calendars -> p95 glyph -> Apply. It should be presets -> calendars -> Apply -> p95 glyph. The glyph is decorative in that flow so should be reached after Apply
Zoe Chen: repro steps: 1) Tab to date range, 2) Enter, 3) Tab through presets -> calendar fields -> Apply. Currently focus lands on glyph before Apply in Chrome 115
Marta Diaz: filed UX-4120: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/UX-4120 for focus order fix and SR readout parity
Riley Gomez: small CSS for glyph mode (semantic-first):

```
.p95-glyph { width:20px; height:20px; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; }
.p95-glyph[role="img"] { outline-offset:2px; }
```

But keep the value in a tooltip and aria-label like `aria-label="95th percentile latency: 198 milliseconds"` — no visually-hidden hacks
Zoe Chen: rendering tweak: add a subtle gaussian blur to heatmap intensity to reduce 'pixelated holes' when density < 25% and draw a 1px stipple pattern overlay for those buckets
Riley Gomez: copy decisions: replace `Show samples` with `Sample density` and subtext `Auto (recommended) | High | Economy` where Auto has a tooltip `Auto: balances accuracy and cost`
Omar Khan: rollout plan: ship UI copy + heatmap stipple behind a feature flag, then phasing in focus-order fix; update docs and add a short note in changelog
Marta Diaz: final accessibility checklist: 1) glyph has aria-label including numeric value, 2) sublabels are exposed to SR when density control focused, 3) focus order corrected in popover, 4) heatmap alt/context explains stipple meaning
Riley Gomez: I'll update the mock with the stipple layer and compact glyph states and drop screens by EOD tomorrow. thanks all! :sparkles:
